claims.claim: A transition that loses the state CAS must not rewrite the terminal state or notify listeners; CancellationTokenTest.losingStateTransitionDoesNotNotifyListeners asserts the state stays CANCELLED and exactly one notification fires.
claims.note: The bind race test uses one start latch for cancel vs bind, not two cancellation transitions; it does not prove first-wins. This test directly asserts the losing transition.

claims.claim: The completedTasks increment must stay last so a converging thread sees the classification, cascade, and fail-fast before it counts a task.
claims.note: Reduced suite TaskGroupConvergenceTest; convergenceSnapshotPublishesEveryMemberClassificationAndTimestamp asserts the snapshot. The earlier larger-suite timeout was not claim-specific.

claims.claim: The cancellation getAndSet(size) can land between the drain loop's range check and getAndIncrement, so the increment observes the phantom index size; handoff's index >= size guard is what prevents tasks.get(size).
claims.proof: The single drain holder reads nextIndex == size-1, so the loop condition passes. Cancellation wins settled and executes nextIndex.getAndSet(size). The holder's getAndIncrement() returns size and stores size+1. Without handoff's index >= size guard, tasks.get(size) is out of bounds. draining admits one claimant, normal claims stop at size, and only the winning cancellation performs getAndSet, so the phantom index is exactly size.
claims.note: The 3000-round stress test did not kill the range-check mutation because the handoff guard is the actual guard; the test is insensitive. A deterministic seam is still needed for dynamic proof.

claims.claim: Reading count before head.next provides the happens-before edge to a concurrent enqueue; reversing the reads can produce a spurious null on a non-empty queue.
claims.proof: Enqueue performs the plain linked-node write last = last.next = node before the volatile read-modify-write on count. A consumer that reads a positive count participates in the volatile write/read pair, so the node link and node initialization happen before its subsequent plain head.next read. Head advancement requires takeMonitor, which peek/poll hold, so a positive count cannot legitimately yield a null first node. Reversing the reads permits: consumer reads head.next == null, producer links the node and increments count, consumer reads the positive count but uses its earlier null.
claims.note: jcstress would be optional dynamic corroboration of a JMM proof, not a prerequisite.

claims.claim: The entire startup (prepare, binds, submit) is one admission against close; a close racing startup cannot retire the deadline scheduler between the group bind and a tighter member bind.
claims.proof: Without the admission, startup can read closed == false, then close can set closed and shut down services while startup is still preparing, binding, or submitting. The real enterAdmission increments first and rechecks closed; a close after the recheck sees a positive admission count and cannot retire services until the matching exit.
claims.note: The earlier mutation removed the increment but left whileOpen's unconditional decrement, so it corrupted activeAdmissions and failed ordinary quiescence tests; that result was a false positive, not proof of the close/startup race.

claims.claim: A true awaitBodyCompletion result must wait until every member observation future carries the final snapshot; removing the observation loop must make a test fail.
claims.note: Real by code review: ScopedCallable publishes body exit, then the member future settles, then the observation listener publishes; a get() waiter can return in between. The cited test waits for the callback to enter before calling awaitBodyCompletion, so it cannot exercise the window; needs a deterministic test.
